rows.statement: Explain common pre-exam instructions (such as removing deodorant or powder and clothing above the waist) and why they matter for image quality.
Build rapport and respond to anxiety, modesty, and physical or cognitive needs while keeping the exam on track.
Explain to a patient in plain language why firm compression improves the image.
Explain the need for a repeat image (for example motion or artifact) honestly and without alarming the patient.
Summarize current ACS and ACR screening recommendations and how they differ from USPSTF guidance.
State the ACS position on breast self-examination and clinical breast examination.
Describe typical mammography dose in patient-friendly terms without overstating or minimizing risk.
Explain the difference between 2D mammography, DBT, and breast ultrasound to a patient.
Tell a patient how and when results reach them and their provider under MQSA.
Explain common reasons for additional imaging after screening without implying a diagnosis.
Distinguish what the technologist may say from what the interpreting physician or provider explains, including density notification.
rows.blockedNote: MQSA covers who receives which report; the technologist's communication scope needs ASRT practice standards (link-only) or equivalent.

rows.statement: Describe breast cancer incidence patterns at the level needed for patient education.
Identify inherent risk factors including reproductive history, age, personal and family history, genetic mutations, prior chest radiation, and breast density.
Identify lifestyle, access-to-care, and hormone-related risk factors, and their implications for imaging history.
Recognize and document signs and symptoms such as pain, lump, nipple discharge, skin thickening, erythema, dimpling, nipple changes, and edema.
Review the imaging request and document surgical history, clinical findings (lumps, scars, moles, tattoos), and gender-affirming care relevant to the exam.
Explain why prior mammograms matter and how to obtain them, including the MQSA transfer timeline.
Define lumpectomy, sentinel node biopsy, simple and modified radical mastectomy, and prophylactic mastectomy.
Define radiation, chemotherapy, hormone therapy, receptor status (ER, PR, HER2), and implant reconstruction.
Explain why mammography uses a low kVp range and how anode material, filtration, window, and focal spot shape the beam.
Describe compression paddle types and MQSA design requirements for paddles, and the role of grids.
Relate SID, OID, and magnification, including the MQSA magnification range requirement.
Identify the components that make up a mammography unit and how they relate along the beam path.
Compare FFDM, DBT, and synthesized 2D imaging.
Describe digital image receptors and the difference between acquisition and interpretation workstations.
Explain HIS/RIS, EMR, and PACS roles, including storage, backup, archive, and basic troubleshooting.
Describe what computer-aided detection does and does not do.
Explain how MQSA certification, accreditation, provisional certificates, and annual inspection fit together.
Describe accreditation clinical image review and the three EQUIP inspection focus areas.
Apply MQSA initial qualification requirements for radiologic technologists, including modality-specific training.
Apply MQSA continuing education, continuing experience, and requalification rules for technologists.
Describe QA program roles (lead interpreting physician, interpreting physicians, medical physicist, QC technologist) and QC record retention.
Identify required report contents and MQSA final and incomplete assessment categories.
Apply MQSA timelines for lay summaries and provider reports, including the 7-day rule for suspicious results and self-referred patients.
Map the four report density categories to the two required patient density statements effective September 10, 2024.
Verify that each image carries the MQSA-required identification, with view and laterality near the axilla.
Apply MQSA retention periods and the 15-day transfer and copy rules for mammograms and reports.
Define and calculate the MQSA medical outcomes audit measures (PPV, cancer detection rate, recall rate).
Apply MQSA requirements for consumer complaints, infection control, and implant inquiry.
Explain the MQSA QC framework: action limits, corrective-action timing, manufacturer QC for digital systems, the phantom dose limit, and compression force limits.
Perform and evaluate the technologist phantom image test (quality and artifacts), including documentation and corrective action.
Describe the compression thickness indicator and compression force tests: purpose, frequency, and criteria.
Use the visual checklist and know what findings require action.
Describe acquisition and interpretation monitor QC (cleanliness, calibration, test patterns such as SMPTE/TG18) and viewing conditions.
Calculate and interpret repeat/reject analysis and identify corrective actions.
Explain the purpose of manufacturer detector calibration.
Explain when the annual physicist survey and a mammography equipment evaluation are required, and what the facility receives.
State the purpose of major physicist tests: collimation, resolution/MTF, SNR/CNR, AEC, artifacts, kVp, HVL, average glandular dose, illuminance, paddle alignment, and workstation QC.
Predict how kVp, mAs, AEC, and manual technique affect contrast, noise, and dose.
Relate compressed thickness, target/filter selection, focal spot, and grid use to image quality and dose.
Explain technique changes for magnification (small focal spot, no grid, air gap).
Evaluate an image against the eight clinical image quality attributes used in accreditation review.
Recognize patient-related artifacts (motion, clothing, overlapping anatomy, implanted devices) and how to prevent them.
Localize findings using clock positions and quadrants for right and left breasts.
Use triangulation between views to estimate lesion location.
Identify external landmarks including breast margins, nipple, areola (Morgagni tubercles, Montgomery glands), skin structures, axillary tail, inframammary fold, and pectoral muscle angle.
Describe fascial layers, retroglandular space, fibroglandular and adipose tissue, Cooper ligaments, pectoral muscle, vessels, and lymphatics.
Describe the terminal ductal lobular unit and its parts, and why it matters in pathology.
Define epithelial cells, myoepithelial cells, and basement membrane, and relate them to in situ versus invasive disease.
Use lexicon descriptors for masses (shape, margin, density), calcifications (typically benign vs suspicious morphology, distribution), asymmetries, and architectural distortion.
Match assessment and density categories to their meaning and typical recommendations.

Describe the typical presentation and mammographic appearance of common benign conditions (cyst, galactocele, fibroadenoma, lipoma, hamartoma, papilloma, duct ectasia, hematoma, abscess, fat necrosis, lymph nodes, gynecomastia, edema, seroma).
Define LCIS, ADH, ALH, papilloma with atypia, flat epithelial atypia, radial scar, and phyllodes tumor, and why upgrade potential matters.
Describe DCIS, invasive ductal and lobular carcinoma, inflammatory carcinoma, Paget disease, sarcoma, lymphoma, and metastases at a technologist level.
Position and evaluate the craniocaudal view against standard criteria.
Position and evaluate the mediolateral oblique view against standard criteria, including pectoral muscle and inframammary fold.
Choose between ML and LM views and explain why the side of interest goes closer to the receptor.
Select XCCL/XCCM, cleavage, and axillary tail views for tissue not shown on standard views.
Use tangential and rolled views to evaluate skin findings and separate superimposed tissue.
Describe implant-displaced views and when they are contraindicated or modified.
Describe nipple-in-profile, anterior compression, spot compression, and magnification views and their purposes.
Ask about implants before the exam and explain the MQSA expectation for views that maximize visible tissue.
Adapt positioning for chest wall variation, kyphosis/lordosis, protruding abdomen, and very large or small breasts (mosaic/tiling, paddle selection).
Adapt imaging for irradiated, reduced, or post-surgical breasts, patients assigned male at birth, implanted devices, and lactation.
Distinguish screening from diagnostic mammography by patient presentation and views.
Describe basic indications and patient preparation for breast ultrasound and MRI.
Prepare a patient for an interventional procedure: pertinent history, informed consent, time-out, setup, and post-procedure instructions.
Describe stereotactic and ultrasound biopsy, wire localization, specimen imaging, and clip placement imaging.
Handle and dispose of specimens, body fluids, sharps, and biopsy supplies safely.
